architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extended the PublicPath type generation to include CSS entrypoints by adding a new helper function getEntrypointPublicExt() that maps entrypoint types to their correct file extensions
architecture_decisions.rationale: The existing implementation only handled HTML and JS entrypoints, but CSS entrypoints (content-script-style and unlisted-style) were missing from type definitions. This caused TypeScript errors when using browser.runtime.getURL() with CSS assets. The new function centralizes the mapping logic and ensures type safety for all supported entrypoint types.
alternatives_considered: Modifying the existing isHtmlEntrypoint() function to also check for CSS types
Adding conditional logic directly in the map() call without a helper function
Creating separate type definitions for CSS assets

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added an end-to-end test to verify CSS entrypoints are correctly included in generated type definitions
architecture_decisions.rationale: E2E testing ensures the type generation works in a real project context, catching integration issues that unit tests might miss. The test creates actual CSS entrypoints and verifies the generated paths.d.ts contains the expected CSS paths. This provides confidence that the fix works for real-world usage.
alternatives_considered: Adding unit tests to the helper function only
Relying on existing type checking without new tests
Creating integration tests at a lower level

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Maintained backward compatibility by extending existing functionality rather than changing the PublicPath type signature
architecture_decisions.rationale: The PublicPath type is generated dynamically based on project entrypoints. By simply adding CSS extensions to the union type, existing code continues to work while new CSS entrypoints gain proper type support. This follows the open-closed principle - extending behavior without modifying existing working code.
alternatives_considered: Changing the PublicPath type to a more generic format
Requiring explicit type annotations for CSS assets

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extracted extension determination logic into a dedicated helper function with clear type annotations
architecture_decisions.rationale: The getEntrypointPublicExt() function provides a single source of truth for mapping entrypoint types to file extensions. The function's return type ('.html' | '.js' | '.css') explicitly documents what extensions are supported. This improves maintainability and makes it easier to add support for new entrypoint types in the future.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the logic inline with the map() call
Using a configuration object or map instead of a switch statement
Placing the function in a separate utility module

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses a gap in the type system where CSS entrypoints (content-script-style and unlisted-style) were not being recognized in the generated PublicPath type definitions. Previously, only HTML and JavaScript entrypoints were included, causing TypeScript errors when developers tried to use browser.runtime.getURL() with CSS assets.

The core change introduces a new helper function getEntrypointPublicExt() that centralizes the logic for determining the public file extension for each entrypoint type. This function uses a switch statement to map entrypoint types to their appropriate extensions (.html, .js, or .css), with CSS support added for the two style entrypoint types. This function is then used in the path generation logic that creates the paths.d.ts type definitions.

The approach maintains backward compatibility while extending type safety to cover all supported entrypoint types. The addition of an E2E test ensures the fix works in a real project context, creating actual CSS entrypoints and verifying they appear correctly in the generated type definitions. This follows the existing patterns in the codebase where type generation is tested through integration tests rather than just unit tests.
